←Module 3: Google Docs
Lesson · 25 min

Creating and Formatting Documents

Start a document, then format text and paragraphs with the toolbar: fonts and sizes, bold and color, alignment, lists and checklists, line spacing, and paint format.

By the end of this lesson you can

  • ✓Create a Google Doc from Drive, the Docs home screen, or a template
  • ✓Change font, size, bold, italic, underline, and text color
  • ✓Align paragraphs and set line and paragraph spacing
  • ✓Make bulleted lists, numbered lists, and checklists
  • ✓Copy formatting with Paint format and remove it with Clear formatting

Lesson Notes

Read through the key concepts before you try the challenge.

Starting a document

On the job

You prepare notices for Parkview's buildings.

The city will shut off the water at Elm Street Apartments for repairs. Marcus typed the notice quickly, and it is one plain block of text. Tenants will skim it on the lobby board, so the time, the date, and what to do must jump out.

Your task: Format the notice so the important information is easy to see.

Name the document right away by clicking Untitled document at the top left. Then just type: there is no Save button, and Saved to Drive shows by the document status icon when your changes are stored.

Formatting text and paragraphs

  • Select first, then format. Click in a paragraph to format the whole paragraph (alignment, spacing, lists); select words to format only those words (bold, color).
  • The same commands are in the Format menu: Format › Text, Format › Align & indent, Format › Line & paragraph spacing, Format › Bullets & numbering.
  • Shortcuts match Word: Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I, Ctrl+U, Ctrl+Shift+E (center), Ctrl+Shift+7 (numbered list), Ctrl+Shift+8 (bulleted list).
  • If the toolbar is too narrow, the rest of the buttons are under More (the three dots) at its right end.

Lists, Paint format, and Clear formatting

  • Bulleted list: select the lines and click Bulleted list. Click the arrow next to it to choose a bullet style.
  • Numbered list: for steps that happen in order.
  • Checklist: each line gets a box you can click to check it off (the text is crossed out).
  • Paint format (the paint roller): click text with the formatting you want, click Paint format, then click or select the text to change. Double-click Paint format to apply it more than once.
  • Clear formatting (Ctrl+\): returns the selected text to plain Normal text.
Worked example

Formatting the water shutoff notice

Make a plain notice readable at a glance on the lobby board.

  1. 1

    Center the title and make it 24 pt.

    Tenants see what the notice is about from across the lobby.

  2. 2

    Bold the sentence with the shutoff time.

    The time is the one fact every tenant needs; bold makes it the first thing the eye lands on.

  3. 3

    Turn the three to-do lines into a bulleted list.

    Lists are faster to skim than a paragraph.

  4. 4

    Set the body to 1.5 line spacing.

    More space between lines is easier to read on a printed notice.

Result: A notice tenants understand in a few seconds.

🔑 Format for the reader: the most important fact should be the easiest to see.

Challenge

Apply what you've learned in this lesson.

Make a notice in your own Google account.

  1. Create a Google Doc named Practice Notice - your name.
  2. Type a title, one sentence with a time and place, and three instructions on their own lines.
  3. Center the title and make it 24 pt. Bold the time and place.
  4. Turn the three instructions into a bulleted list, and set the document to 1.5 line spacing.
  5. Add a checklist of two items at the end, and check one off.
Deliverable: Submit your notice as a PDF (File › Download › PDF Document) or share it with your instructor as a Viewer. No Google account? Complete the practice simulation and submit its results page.
